short.q: Describe the difference between Component 1 and Component 2.
short.model: Component 1 is a project on a theme set by the teacher (or agreed with them) with coursework studies and a final outcome. Component 2 starts from a Cambridge question paper, with supporting studies and an 8-hour supervised final outcome.
points: Component 1: theme, studies and final outcome over the course
Component 2: Cambridge starting point, supporting studies, 8-hour test

short.q: What does the AO2 band 'confident' require compared with 'competent'?
short.model: 'Confident' means consistently selecting relevant resources and exploring media, materials, techniques and processes confidently; 'competent' shows clear selection. The key difference is consistency.
points: explores media, techniques and processes with confidence

short.q: Give two ways to improve AO1 marks in a sketchbook.
short.model: Record from a variety of first-hand sources such as your own drawings, photographs and gallery sketches, and state your intentions clearly as the work progresses.
points: variety of relevant sources including first-hand

short.q: Explain why selection is important in AO2.
short.model: AO2 asks you to explore and select. Trying media is not enough; you must choose the most suitable one and show why, which proves judgement.

short.q: Name two rules about the two components' work.
short.model: The work must be your own, presented as a digital portfolio, and work for Component 2 must not be the same as work submitted for Component 1.
